cases.purpose: Default inventory is the literal authenticated old79 plus only git; absent optional/default-node/npm/npx distinctions remain.
Root/subpath factories and plugin are callable through actual package exports; public declarations agree, not a source-relative fallback.
Standalone Git plugin works without aggregate; duplicate registration rejects; explicit top-level replacement works and nested aggregate replacement cannot bypass it.
discoveryBoundary changes repository discovery only; unknown/numeric cap overrides reject without mutation; all24 accepted module constants remain byte-bound.
Loose neutral repository: root Git status/log/show/ls-files and raw blob bytes through real virtual-shell pipelines; exact fixture expectations frozen independently.
Packed neutral repository including accepted OFS/REF delta fixtures: public routes yield the same independently specified logical objects without native Git execution.
apply_patch modifies a tracked virtual worktree file; Git status/diff detects exact effect while object/index bytes stay unchanged.
Shell arrays preserve a literal path with spaces and option-looking text into Git argv; quoting and -- behavior use accepted parser semantics.
Readonly wrapper permits inspection and rejects a surrounding attempted mutation; Git itself performs no write, including error paths.
Middleware observes public Git argv/cwd/ByteIO routing and exact dispatch count without changing repository content or inventing host authority.
Corrupt/missing packed and loose metadata returns the specified non-success result, never a false clean status; ordinary stderr/status and Shell rejection boundaries remain distinct.
Output failure/abort closes owned shell scopes with exact reason and no retry; lifecycle credit limited to actual observable registrations, not private native allocation.

membershipQualification: Twelve bounded preparation families, not twelve fully specified runnable cases or semantic passes. Exact input/output bytes and conditional cleanup criteria must be committed before execution.
